item.title: You Probably Do Not Need a VPN
item.description:
tl;dr: Enable “Always use HTTPS” and then use Tor if needed. Use Public WiFi without fear with/without a VPN.

I have been more privacy conscious over time and while it is evolving, my threat model has mostly stayed the same: A criminal looking to exploit my devices/data. My decisions revolve around this and I always make sure it makes a lot of sense in that context. One of those decisions is to NOT use a VPN.

item.title: Why I Use Podman over Docker
item.description:
If you ever start self-hosting, there is a very good chance you will be encouraged to use containers. That’s for good reason. In general, it is better to containerize something if you can. Containers are kind of like a miniature VM: It makes sure dependencies run smoothly without having to worry about different Containers messing each other’s files.

Docker is usually the go-to tool for this but I recommend people to just go to Podman. I have started with Docker and even appreciated Docker Compose but there are several reasons I decided to move.

item.title: Software Minimalism
item.description:
In my journey to become a minimalist, one of the things that I fail to apply the knowledge to is Software. But as my relationship with technology has evolved, I realized it is something that needs culling.

Earlier this year, I downgraded my phone from an iPhone 14 Pro Max to a Samsung A56 5G. That said, I cannot really call it a downgrade in a traditional sense since I just moved into a phone that actually served my needs.

item.title: Podman, Caddy, and Lego: DNS-01 Challenges without having to use xCaddy
item.description:
Caddy is great and one of the main benefits it has is the automatic SSL. Unfortunately, that fails when I needed DNS challenges. The common solution is to rebuild Caddy with the proper plugins but I didn’t like this as it meant I had to watch out for updates. There are also unofficial builds but I don’t want to risk that.

This got me exploring other ways to get the certificates through Let’s Encrypt. I scrolled through their ACME clients and got into Lego.

item.title: How I Archive
item.description:
One thing I discovered over the years: I generate a TON of files. A lot of these files are trash and do not need to be referenced in the future. But there are some that I feel iffy about deleting - or even just not really a good idea.

These include:

  1. Past Projects whose architecture I might want to reference 2. Photos of old documents 3. Software I purchased which is in danger of just not being available on the internet anymore in the future

For these files, I archive them. And over the few years I started doing so, I optimized it.
